name: The Movielife
label: Revelation
lede: A Long Island band that fed guitarists to Taking Back Sunday, Bayside and Brand New, crashed two vans, made one record for Revelation that still gets repressed, and quit at the top so its singer could go lay tile.

eras.title: The Long Island revolving door
eras.text: The Movielife started in 1997 with Vinnie Caruana singing and a line-up that would not sit still. Guitarists and bassists kept leaving to start bands that became bigger than the one they left, and by the end of 1999 Caruana had a steady crew, two demos and a debut album on Fadeaway Records.

years.h: The Movielife forms on Long Island
years.p: Vinnie Caruana sings, Alex Amiruddin and [[Eddie Reyes|906bf563-38b6-44d0-bb8e-e81f83159ce8]] play guitar, Nick Ghanbarian plays bass and Evan Baken drums. They cut the Red Demo with producer [[Mike Sapone|96e6e404-ba70-427a-9db9-60019fa6e021]].

years.h: Eddie Reyes leaves The Movielife, heads for Taking Back Sunday
years.p: Guitarist Eddie Reyes quits to start Runner Up, then joins [[Taking Back Sunday|350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d]]. His replacement, Dave O'Connell, leaves soon after to form Quick Fix Kills.

years.h: Brandon Reilly arrives from the Rookie Lot; Nick Ghanbarian leaves
years.p: Guitarist [[Brandon Reilly|1016f8b6-7ed0-43e7-ab4d-0b71bb18c342]] comes from Levittown's the Rookie Lot, whose other members went on to form [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]]. Bassist Nick Ghanbarian leaves for [[Bayside|5f821136-9935-403c-abb5-e78ddda35e9f]] and Phil Navetta takes over.

years.h: The Movielife's White Demo lands them on Fadeaway Records
years.p: The Movielife's second demo, known as the White Demo, gets Fadeaway Records interested, and the band signs its first record deal.

years.h: It's Go Time, The Movielife's debut · Fadeaway
years.p: The Movielife's first album comes out on Fadeaway Records, and the band hits the road hard behind it.

eras.title: One record for Revelation
eras.text: The Movielife almost signed with Equal Vision and went to Revelation instead. The one album they made there, This Time Next Year, is the record the band's fans still wear out; it was also the start of a touring life that nearly killed them in North Dakota.

years.h: The Movielife pick Revelation over Equal Vision
years.p: With crowds growing, The Movielife come close to signing with Equal Vision Records, then sign with Revelation Records instead.

years.h: This Time Next Year · Revelation REV 97
years.p: Recorded with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] at Salad Days Studio in Washington, D.C. Revelation's first vinyl run is 750 on blue and 900 on black.
years.xp: Demand never went away. Revelation's pressing history lists represses in 2010 (white, red and black), 548 on gold in 2014, 330 on clear in 2015 and 550 on opaque green in 2016.

years.h: The Movielife wreck their van in North Dakota
years.p: Touring with Reach the Sky and [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], The Movielife crash their van in North Dakota and have to drop off the tour.

years.h: The Movielife tour with Glassjaw, then Reel Big Fish
years.p: In spring The Movielife tour with [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] and Autopilot Off. In July and August they open the Reel Big Fish and Goldfinger co-headlining run.

years.h: A Movielife tour with Finch is called off after 9/11
years.p: A September 2001 tour with [[Finch|746737be-e792-42bb-b18c-fb46d7935d7a]] and [[The Starting Line|9701356d-08d9-45ba-975d-977ab466e7be]] is cancelled after the September 11 attacks.

years.h: Has a Gambling Problem EP: The Movielife move to Drive-Thru
years.p: Having signed with Drive-Thru Records, The Movielife release the Has a Gambling Problem EP, then close the year supporting [[Good Charlotte|b267ca80-034e-4dc1-9ed4-ec45f1fed41d]] and [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]].

eras.title: Forty hours and out
eras.text: The Movielife's last two years were the busiest of their life: Warped Tour, Europe, a Billboard album and another van crash. A founding guitarist walked because he hated where the music was going, and eighteen months later the whole band ended with a note on its website.

years.big: One founder out. A Navetta brother in.
q: grew disenchanted with the new direction of the music
years.h: Alex Amiruddin quits The Movielife over its new sound
years.p: Founding guitarist Alex Amiruddin leaves The Movielife and starts Keep Breathing. Phil Navetta's younger brother, Dan Navetta, takes his place.
years.xp:
Amiruddin said he had grown disenchanted with the direction the music was taking. The Movielife were on Drive-Thru by then, opening for Good Charlotte and the Mighty Mighty Bosstones, and about to spend the summer on Warped Tour.

Amiruddin later joined Wiretap Crash in 2011.

years.h: The Movielife play the Deconstruction Tour and Warped
years.p: The Movielife cross Europe on the Deconstruction Tour in May and June 2002, then spend June to August on the Warped Tour.

years.h: The Movielife tour the US with Brand New
years.p: The Movielife head out with [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]], The Reunion Show and Orange Island. Brand New's line-up included three of Brandon Reilly's old bandmates from the Rookie Lot.

years.h: Forty Hour Train Back to Penn hits the Billboard 200
years.p: The Movielife's third album, on Drive-Thru, peaks at No. 164 on the Billboard 200. In May they shoot a video for Jamestown with Digital Kitchen.
play: Forty Hour Train Back to Penn

years.h: Drummer Evan Baken is hurt in a second Movielife van crash
years.p: Evan Baken is injured in a van accident, and The Movielife bring in a fill-in drummer for their UK tour.

years.h: The Movielife break up with a note on their website
years.p: After the Made Tour and a Hellfest slot, The Movielife announce the split online. The Pitch reported Vinnie Caruana said goodbye to about 3,000 fans at the farewell show.
years.xp:
Nobody gave a clean reason. Caruana later told Vice that bands break up in the heat of the moment, and that The Movielife were young and ran into a wall.

Two days after the split, The Pitch reported, Caruana was working demolition on a New York construction site. He also laid tile, and said going back to construction was no good.

eras.title: Avalanches and nightmares
eras.text: Vinnie Caruana and Brandon Reilly went separate ways, into I Am the Avalanche and Nightmare of You. The Movielife songs kept turning up anyway, first as acoustic one-offs, then as a reunion that came too early.

years.h: Vinnie Caruana and Brandon Reilly play Movielife songs acoustic
years.p: A year after the split, Caruana and Reilly reunite for an acoustic set of Movielife songs. By then Caruana is building [[I Am the Avalanche|8e8e27cb-8553-496e-98bc-67bbd72e98dc]] and Reilly fronts [[Nightmare of You|32efc6ae-edf6-4fd1-b268-226073db9a36]].

years.h: Set Your Goals back Vinnie Caruana for a Movielife set at Bamboozle
years.p: At the Bamboozle festival in New Jersey, Vinnie Caruana sings a set of Movielife songs with [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]] as his band.

years.h: A YouTube video announces The Movielife's return
years.p: Vinnie Caruana and Brandon Reilly announce in a YouTube video that The Movielife will play Bamboozle in New Jersey, their first show in nearly eight years.

q: I don't think I was ready.
years.h: The Movielife's first reunion fizzles after Bamboozle
years.p: The Movielife play Bamboozle and a New York show in August, then stop again. Vinnie Caruana later said neither he nor Brandon Reilly was ready.

eras.title: Afraid of drugs, and back for real
eras.text: The second reunion started as two old friends hanging out with Brandon Reilly's son. It turned into rehearsals three days a week, a return at Irving Plaza, the first new Movielife song in thirteen years and, in 2017, a full album as a trio.

years.h: The Movielife start rehearsing three days a week
years.p: Vinnie Caruana and Brandon Reilly reconnect as friends, and the 2003 line-up, with the Navetta brothers and Evan Baken, starts rehearsing three days a week.

years.h: The Movielife come back at Irving Plaza
years.p: The Movielife play New York's Irving Plaza, their first show since 2011. UK dates follow in June at London's Electric Ballroom, Birmingham and Manchester.

years.h: Future Feeling (Afraid of Drugs): new Movielife music
years.p: Vice premieres Future Feeling (Afraid of Drugs), The Movielife's first new song in thirteen years.

years.h: The Movielife slim down to a trio with drummer Brett Romnes
years.p: Promo photos after the 2016 election show only Vinnie Caruana, Brandon Reilly and new drummer Brett Romnes.

years.h: Cities in Search of a Heart · Rise Records
years.p: The Movielife's fourth album, and first in fourteen years, comes out on Rise Records. The band plays Slam Dunk Festival in the UK the same year.

years.h: The Movielife tour with New Found Glory
years.p: The Movielife support [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] across the US on the Sick Tour, seventeen years after the two bands first toured together.

years.h: Vinnie Caruana: more Movielife is up to Brandon Reilly
years.p: On the Podioslave podcast, Vinnie Caruana says he wouldn't be surprised by more Movielife music, but Brandon Reilly has to write it.
